sealed: Written and committed before the recorder, the log, the normaliser, the importer or tools/measure-2.mjs existed. tools/measure-2.mjs refuses to run if this file differs from the commit that sealed it. A claim that fails is kept.
what: Organ 2, capture. A recorder that sits on Claude Code's hooks and writes the job down as it happens: the intent sealed with `acg seal` before the first prompt; each prompt (the start of model work), each tool use (name and a hash of its input) and each file read or written (by hash, a copy kept) appended to a log in which every line carries the hash of the line before. Notes the agent or person adds (`acg note` assumption, question, answer, approval, intervention, verification, re-run, acceptance, claim) go in the same log. A normaliser turns the log into a schema-v1 record, its summary written from the log. An importer turns a past Claude Code transcript into a record, so finished jobs can be judged too. The recorder never blocks the harness: on any error it exits cleanly and writes the error to its own file. Claude Code's hooks fire on prompts and tool uses, not on each model request, so a live record marks each prompt as the start of model work; the importer, which reads the transcript, records each model request.
data: Real jobs: every Claude Code transcript on this machine (under ~/.claude/projects) of at most 30 MB with between 1 and 300 tool uses in its main thread — 31 at sealing, counted by number of tool uses only; no content was read out. Subagent (side-chain) lines are left out of both paths alike. The transcripts are private: they are read on this machine, and the receipt holds only counts and hashes, never text, paths or tool names.
seenBefore: Only the number of transcripts and their tool-use counts (to choose the bound). Nothing has been recorded, imported or judged.
scope: The live path is driven by replaying each transcript's prompts and tool uses into the hook command — a separate process per event, its input the JSON Claude Code's hooks deliver — not by a live Claude Code session. That Claude Code calls the hook once per prompt and per tool use is its documented behaviour, not measured here.

claims.claim: Import is faithful: for every transcript, the imported record holds exactly its main-thread tool uses, in order and by name, and one model call per distinct model request; and every imported record fits the strict schema (P0 passes).

The live path matches: replaying every transcript into the hook command gives a record whose tool uses are the import's, same names and same order; its log verifies line by line; and it fits the strict schema.
Intent first, by construction: for every transcript replay, sealing the intent before the first prompt makes P1 pass on the hook record, and sealing it after the first prompt makes P1 fail.
Capture is cheap: across all hook events of all replays, the hook process takes a median of at most 150 ms and a 95th percentile of at most 400 ms of wall time on this machine.
The log is tamper-evident: changing one field of a line, removing a line, or swapping two adjacent lines of any replay's log is caught by the log check, for every such edit tried (up to 200 per log).

The recorder never breaks the harness: 500 garbage hook inputs (not JSON, the wrong shape, fields missing) each exit cleanly within 2 seconds, add nothing to any job's log, and leave a line in the recorder's error file.
A past job is never dressed up: every imported transcript, having no sealed intent, fails P1.
